questions.q: According to the chapter, which success factor is one of the easiest for a tourism business to control?
options: The weather
Customer service levels
Exchange rates
Competitors' prices
questions.explain: Service quality is measured with tools like Net Promoter Score and customer lifetime value.
questions.evidence: one of the easiest to control is customer service levels.

questions.q: Why is an airline flight an example of an intangible service?
options: It cannot be refunded
It is sold online
It is too expensive to sample
It is bought in advance and not experienced until the customer is on the plane
questions.explain: Customers can't see or test a service before paying, which raises the importance of trust.
questions.evidence: An airplane flight is an example of an intangible service because a customer purchases it in advance and doesn’t “experience” or “consume” the product until he or she is on the plane.

questions.q: What is total quality management (TQM) in tourism and hospitality?
options: A process where the entire team creates service expectations, with management and employees collaborating
A system for inspecting rooms
A government quality licence
A discount programme for loyal guests
questions.explain: Service quality is everyone's job, not only management's.
questions.evidence: Total quality management (TQM) in tourism and hospitality is a process where service expectations are created by the entire team, with a collaborative approach between management and employees

questions.q: Are positive personal attributes enough for staff to deliver great customer engagements?
options: Yes, personality is all that matters
Only for senior staff
Not necessarily — staff also need specific training toward customer orientation
Only in large hotels
questions.explain: Training and certifications help make remarkable service consistent.
questions.evidence: Even when employees have positive attributes, it may not be enough to ensure positive customer engagements unless they are specifically trained toward customer orientation

questions.q: Why are organisations increasingly focused on retaining existing customers?
options: New customers are not allowed
It is often less expensive than attracting new ones
Loyal customers pay higher prices by law
It removes the need for marketing
questions.explain: Loyalty programmes and great service build long-term relationships.
questions.evidence: organizations are increasingly focusing on retaining existing customers, which is often less expensive than attracting new ones.

questions.q: What should you do with the feedback you get from user support?
options: Delete it after a month
Share it only with the legal team
Use it to set staff bonuses only
Use it to decide how you'll improve your service
questions.explain: Support contacts reveal where the service confuses people.
questions.evidence: You should use feedback you get from user support to decide how you’ll improve your service.

questions.q: What must a service team make sure of, according to the assisted digital guidance?
options: That everyone who needs the service can use it
That every user applies online without help
That paper forms are abolished
That support is only available by email
questions.explain: Assisted digital support helps people who can't use the online service on their own.
questions.evidence: You must make sure everyone who needs your service can use it.

questions.q: What does point 7 on the digital inclusion scale represent?
options: Expert programmers
People who have never used a computer
Users with basic digital skill — the minimum needed to use the internet effectively
People without a phone
questions.explain: Research why some users avoid digital services or choose other channels.
questions.evidence: Point 7 on the scale represents users with ‘basic digital skill’ - this is the minimum ability that people need to have in order to use the internet effectively.

questions.q: Why bring different service channels (online, phone, face to face) together?
options: To close the cheaper channels
To design an experience that makes sense to the user, however they use the service
To reduce the number of staff
To make every user switch to online
questions.explain: Users shouldn't get an inferior experience because they lack technology or skills.
questions.evidence: Bringing different channels together means you can design an experience that makes sense to the user, however they use the service.

questions.q: When must you let users tell you what they think of your online service?
options: Only when they complain
Only once a year in a survey
Before they start using it
Once they've finished using it
questions.explain: Also allow feedback at various stages of the journey.
questions.evidence: You must allow users to tell you what they think of your service once they’ve finished using it.
